requirements.description: Identify PMB and preserve distinct analytes, formulations, routes, concentration bases and biological matrices for each nonhuman record.
conditions: A conversion or physiological bridge needs recorded justification.

evidence.quote: Use PMB as the sole test drug; do not substitute colistin or another antibiotic.

Keep PMB routes, formulations, analytes, total and unbound drug, and plasma, serum, whole-lung tissue, BAL and ELF distinct. Record justification for each conversion or physiological bridge; do not force unsupported pulmonary or multi-species models.

requirements.description: Preserve source identity, units, observation origin, missing values and BLQ limits without assigning individual animals or cross-time links to summaries.
conditions: Group means and digitized observations retain their reported data level.
An unspecified identifier or censoring bound remains unresolved.

evidence.quote: Preserve source identifiers, units, missing values and BLQ limits. Group means and digitized observations are not individual animals; do not invent IDs, variability, exposure-response links or missing measurements.

Treat the separate mouse digitized index-response panels as unmatched until supported regimen-to-response links are established. Do not invent exposure-response links or individual animals from digitized observations or group means.

requirements.description: Define each animal PK observation's time and concentration, dosing events and study or regimen membership at its actual data level.
conditions: Retain actual versus nominal sampling times where relevant.
Record infusion or repeated-dose input history when it affects the requested time course or exposure window.
An optional NCA analysis does not precede animal model preparation.

evidence.quote: Test whether animal PK and preclinical PK/PD can predict human polymyxin B exposure and support efficacious-dose estimation; the primary outcome is model feasibility.

Animal PK work will select eligible systemic and, where supported, pulmonary models for mouse, rat and rabbit; evaluate fit, parameter identifiability and held-out prediction where the design permits; and limit rabbit use to evidence that identifies a model component, documenting exclusion or exploratory use otherwise (MI003, MI004). The rabbit source-preservation requirement is SC32.

requirements.description: Preserve the distinct mouse and rat binding estimates and define the unbound-fraction sensitivity inputs used for eligible free-exposure work.
conditions: Apply when an index or target uses free exposure.
Keep conflicting estimates separate rather than averaging them.
Directly measured unbound concentrations have their own stated basis.

evidence.quote: Preserve the conflicting mouse binding estimates of about 91% versus 97–99% bound and rat estimates of 80% versus 92–99%. Do not average them; carry unbound fraction as a sensitivity parameter.

The proposal reports conflicting protein-binding sources: mouse approximately 91% versus 97–99% bound, and rat 80% versus 92–99%. Do not average them; carry unbound fraction (fu) as a sensitivity parameter (MI002).

requirements.description: Identify K. pneumoniae strain-specific MIC inputs for MIC-normalized indices and target work, retaining susceptibility context.
conditions: Apply to MIC-normalized indices or an MIC threshold.
The surveillance MIC distribution cannot replace matched strain MICs.
Other organisms cannot define K. pneumoniae targets.

evidence.quote: Use eligible K. pneumoniae time-kill data for PD and the surveillance MIC distribution for population-weighted attainment; the distribution cannot replace matched strain MICs.

Give fAUC/MIC, fCmax/MIC and fT>MIC equal eligibility and compare ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill models on the same matched K. pneumoniae response records, strain MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, windows and likelihood. Register selection criteria before fitting; report R², AIC/BIC, stability and identifiability, count the extra Hill parameter, and do not select by R² alone or force a winner.
Keep K. pneumoniae stasis, 1-log kill and 2-log kill targets separate; do not use other pathogens to set those targets.

requirements.description: Establish supported links among each eligible K. pneumoniae response record, regimen, strain MIC, exposure basis and observation window.
conditions: Separate digitized mouse index-response panels remain unmatched until links are supported.
Within-panel target inputs and common-record cross-index comparison have distinct pairing requirements.
Do not create pairs by row order or infer individuals from group summaries.

evidence.quote: Treat the separate mouse digitized index-response panels as unmatched until supported regimen-to-response links are established. Do not invent exposure-response links or individual animals from digitized observations or group means.

Give fAUC/MIC, fCmax/MIC and fT>MIC equal eligibility and compare ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill models on the same matched K. pneumoniae response records, strain MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, windows and likelihood. Register selection criteria before fitting; report R², AIC/BIC, stability and identifiability, count the extra Hill parameter, and do not select by R² alone or force a winner.

Give all three indices equal eligibility and use both regression families. Compare them on the same matched response records, strain MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, time windows and likelihood.

requirements.description: Define the candidate free-exposure indices and the common comparison basis for eligible K. pneumoniae response records.
conditions: Give all three specified indices equal eligibility.
Define whether fT>MIC is a duration or percentage.
A common comparison requires compatible records, windows and likelihood definitions.

evidence.quote: Give fAUC/MIC, fCmax/MIC and fT>MIC equal eligibility and compare ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill models on the same matched K. pneumoniae response records, strain MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, windows and likelihood. Register selection criteria before fitting; report R², AIC/BIC, stability and identifiability, count the extra Hill parameter, and do not select by R² alone or force a winner.

Give all three indices equal eligibility and use both regression families. Compare them on the same matched response records, strain MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, time windows and likelihood.

requirements.description: Define each K. pneumoniae target effect separately through its bacterial-burden endpoint, reference and observation time.
conditions: Retain separate definitions for stasis, 1-log kill and 2-log kill.
An endpoint definition is an input to target estimation, not an estimated target value.

evidence.quote: Keep K. pneumoniae stasis, 1-log kill and 2-log kill targets separate; do not use other pathogens to set those targets.
Keep stasis, 1-log kill and 2-log kill targets separate; other pathogens cannot set K. pneumoniae targets.

requirements.description: Retain the infection or in-vitro experiment context and response observations needed to interpret a matched index comparison or target estimate.
conditions: Apply to response-linked index comparison or new target estimation.
Preserve separate experimental contexts and response windows.
A reported target considered for use has a separate source and applicability definition; raw response data are not automatically required solely to register it.

evidence.quote: Test whether animal PK and preclinical PK/PD can predict human polymyxin B exposure and support efficacious-dose estimation; the primary outcome is model feasibility.

For eligible K. pneumoniae data, the project will compare fAUC/MIC, fCmax/MIC and fT>MIC using ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill regression, then estimate supported exposure targets or report that the available data cannot determine a best index or target (MI009, MI010).
